title: Greater Glory: More Than Success
description:
## Greater Glory: More Than Success

When I first thought about this year’s Refreshing theme, “Greater Glory,” my mind didn’t immediately go to bright lights, recognition, or applause. Instead, I thought about growth.

Growth is often quiet. It happens in the unseen moments, the long nights of studying, the extra hours spent learning a skill, the failures that nobody celebrates, and the prayers whispered when no one is watching. Yet, these are the very moments God uses to prepare us for greater things.

As students, it’s easy to believe that glory is something waiting for us after graduation or when we finally get our dream jobs. But God doesn’t only reveal His glory at the destination; He reveals it throughout the journey.

As someone in the media and creative space, I’ve learned that every piece of work tells a story. Whether it’s a photograph, a video, a design, or even a simple social media post, something is always being communicated. The question is, what story are we telling?

We live in a generation where everyone wants to be seen, but not everyone wants to grow. We chase visibility, but God is more interested in building capacity. Before He gives influence, He develops character. Before He brings people to notice us, He teaches us faithfulness.

I’ve come to realise that excellence is one of the simplest ways we honour God. Excellence isn’t about having the most expensive camera or the latest laptop. It’s about giving your best with whatever God has placed in your hands. A student who prepares diligently for an exam glorifies God. A designer who pays attention to details glorifies God. A writer who communicates truth with wisdom glorifies God. A leader who serves with humility glorifies God.

Sometimes we become discouraged because someone else seems to be moving faster than we are. Social media doesn’t help either. It constantly reminds us of what others are achieving. But God’s timetable has never depended on comparison. The process you’re in today may be preparing you for responsibilities you cannot yet see.

One thing the creative industry has taught me is that every professional was once a beginner. Nobody starts at the top. Every expert has stories of mistakes, rejected ideas, failed attempts, and lessons learned. Growth is part of the process, and God is never intimidated by our small beginnings.

As Baptist students, we have an opportunity to stand out, not just because of what we know, but because of who we represent. Our society need students whose integrity matches their intelligence, whose excellence reflects their faith, and whose lives point others to Christ.

The world already has enough people chasing success. What it needs are people whose success carries purpose.

Perhaps that is what Greater Glory truly looks like. It is becoming more like Christ while becoming better at what He has called us to do. It is allowing our gifts, our studies, our careers, and even our daily interactions to reflect Him.

As we gather for Refreshing this year, my prayer is that we won’t simply leave inspired. I pray we leave transformed, ready to grow, ready to serve, and ready to glorify God in every lecture hall, every workplace, every ministry, and every opportunity He brings our way.

Because in the end, the greatest glory is not that people know our names, but that through our lives, they come to know Christ.

---

**Yours truly,**

**Adebisi Taiwo Mercy**

title: Financial Wisdom for Students: A Guide to Managing Money in School
description:
## Financial Wisdom for Students: A Guide to Managing Money in School

### Introduction

One of the greatest challenges many students face is not academics but financial management. While in school, students often receive money from parents, guardians, scholarships, part-time jobs, or other sources. Without proper planning, this money can be spent quickly, leading to unnecessary stress and financial difficulties.

Financial literacy is the ability to understand and manage money effectively. Developing this skill as a student can help you meet your needs, achieve your goals, and prepare for a successful future.

### Understanding Your Financial Situation

The first step toward financial stability is knowing how much money comes in and how much goes out. Students should identify their sources of income and list their regular expenses such as:

- School fees
- Accommodation
- Feeding
- Transportation
- Internet subscription
- Books and study materials
- Personal care

Keeping track of income and expenses helps students make informed financial decisions.

### The Importance of Budgeting

A budget is a financial plan that outlines how money will be spent over a specific period. Budgeting helps students avoid wasteful spending and ensures that important needs are met.

**Steps to Create a Budget:**
- Calculate your total income.
- List all expected expenses.
- Prioritize needs over wants.
- Allocate money to each expense category.
- Review and adjust your budget regularly.

A student who follows a budget is less likely to experience financial shortages before the end of the semester.

### Distinguishing Between Needs and Wants

- Many financial problems arise when students confuse needs with wants.
- Needs are necessities required for survival and academic success, such as food, accommodation, textbooks, and transportation.
- Wants are things that make life more enjoyable but are not essential, such as expensive gadgets, luxury clothing, and excessive entertainment.
- Wise students learn to satisfy their needs first before spending on wants.

### Developing a Saving Habit

Saving is not only for working-class individuals; students should also cultivate the habit of saving. Even small amounts saved consistently can become significant over time.

**Benefits of saving include:**
- Emergency preparedness
- Funding future projects
- Reducing dependence on others
- Building financial discipline
- A simple rule is to save a portion of every amount received before spending.
- Avoiding Unnecessary Debt

### Beware of Financial Scams

Students are often targets of fraudulent schemes promising quick wealth and unrealistic returns.

**To protect yourself:**
- Avoid "get-rich-quick" schemes.
- Verify investment opportunities.
- Never share sensitive banking information.
- Be cautious of online fraud and phishing messages.

### Exploring Legitimate Sources of Income

Students can improve their financial situation through legitimate activities such as:
- Freelancing
- Tutoring
- Graphic design
- Content writing
- Photography
- Campus-based businesses
- Internship opportunities

These activities not only provide income but also help students develop valuable skills.

### Setting Financial Goals

Financial goals provide direction and motivation. Students should establish both short-term and long-term goals.

**Examples include:**
- Saving for a laptop
- Paying for professional courses
- Starting a small business
- Building an emergency fund
- Goals help students stay focused and avoid impulsive spending.

### Conclusion

Financial management is a vital life skill that every student should develop. By budgeting wisely, saving consistently, avoiding unnecessary debt, and making informed financial decisions, students can enjoy a more stable and productive academic journey. The habits formed during school years often shape future financial success. Therefore, students should view financial literacy not as an option but as a necessity for achieving both academic and personal goals.

"Do not save what is left after spending, but spend what is left after saving." This principle can help every student build a secure financial future.

title: Friendship: Choosing the Right Companions for a Fulfilling Life
description:
## FRIENDSHIP: CHOOSING THE RIGHT COMPANIONS FOR A FULFILLING LIFE

Friendship is one of God's greatest gifts to humanity. No one is designed to live in isolation. From the beginning of creation, God declared, "It is not good that the man should be alone" (Genesis 2:18). Although this statement was made concerning marriage, the principle extends to human relationships. Every individual needs people who will encourage, correct, support, and strengthen them.

The quality of our friends determines, to a large extent, the quality of our lives. Proverbs 13:20 says, "He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed." This timeless truth reminds us that friendships either build us up or pull us down. Good friends draw us closer to God and help us become better versions of ourselves, while unhealthy friendships can gradually destroy our faith, character, and destiny.

**Below are five kinds of friends every believer should cultivate.**

### 1. Friends Who Help You Stay Grateful - 1 Thessalonians 5:18
*"In everything give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you."*

Life presents many reasons to complain. Financial difficulties, disappointments, delayed expectations, family challenges, and health concerns can easily rob us of our joy. During such moments, the friends around us become very important.

A grateful friend constantly reminds you of God's goodness instead of magnifying your problems. Such friends help you remember past victories, answered prayers, and God's faithfulness. Rather than encouraging bitterness and self-pity, they redirect your focus to God's unfailing love.

The Israelites repeatedly complained in the wilderness despite experiencing miraculous deliverance from Egypt. Their negative attitude prevented many of them from entering the Promised Land. In contrast, David consistently encouraged himself in the Lord even during difficult seasons.

**Friends who cultivate gratitude help you:**
- Count your blessings instead of your losses.
- See opportunities in challenges.
- Maintain joy despite difficult circumstances.
- Develop contentment while trusting God for greater things.
- Live with hope and confidence in God's promises.

A thankful heart attracts God's presence and opens the door for greater blessings. Therefore, choose friends who remind you to praise God rather than complain endlessly.

### 2. Friends Who Inspire Excellence - Proverbs 27:17
*"Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend."*

God never intended friendship to promote mediocrity. True friends challenge one another to improve continually. Just as iron sharpens iron through contact, genuine friends sharpen each other's minds, skills, attitudes, and spiritual lives. They celebrate your success but also challenge you not to settle for average performance.

Excellent friends encourage diligence, discipline, integrity, and continuous learning. They correct you lovingly when necessary and celebrate your progress without envy.

Daniel and his companions inspired one another to remain faithful in Babylon despite immense pressure to compromise. Their commitment to excellence caused them to stand above every other official in the kingdom.

**Friends who inspire excellence will:**
- Encourage hard work.
- Promote honesty and integrity.
- Challenge you to pursue your God-given potential.
- Celebrate your achievements sincerely.
- Motivate you to improve spiritually, academically, and professionally.

Avoid friends who constantly discourage your dreams or encourage laziness. The right friendship stretches your capacity and brings out the best in you.

### 3. Friends Who Shape Your Character and Conversation - Ephesians 4:31
*"Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice."*

Character determines destiny, and conversations reveal character. Our speech reflects the condition of our hearts. The friends we spend time with influence the way we speak, think, behave, and respond to situations.

Negative friendships often normalize gossip, anger, slander, dishonesty, immoral jokes, and destructive habits. Over time, these attitudes become part of one's lifestyle.

On the other hand, godly friends encourage words that build rather than destroy. They correct harmful behavior in love and inspire purity, kindness, forgiveness, humility, and patience.

The Bible warns in 1 Corinthians 15:33: *"Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners."*

**Good friends help us:**
- Speak words of encouragement.
- Avoid gossip and slander.
- Practice forgiveness.
- Develop patience and humility.
- Maintain integrity in public and private.

A person's future is greatly influenced by the company they keep. Therefore, surround yourself with people whose words reflect the character of Christ.

### 4. Friends Who Strengthen Your Faith in God

Faith grows in the company of believers who genuinely love God. There are moments when our faith becomes weak because of trials, unanswered prayers, disappointments, or prolonged waiting. During such seasons, godly friends become instruments of God's encouragement.

Jonathan strengthened David's hand in God when King Saul sought to kill him (1 Samuel 23:16). Rather than discouraging David, Jonathan reminded him of God's promise concerning the throne of Israel.

**Friends who strengthen your faith will:**
- Pray with you and for you.
- Encourage you with Scripture.
- Remind you of God's promises.
- Help you remain committed to church fellowship.
- Correct you when your decisions contradict God's Word.

Such friends do not simply sympathize with your pain—they point you back to Christ.

Hebrews 10:24–25 encourages believers to provoke one another unto love and good works and not neglect gathering together. Spiritual friendships create accountability and perseverance. Choose companions who make you love God more, not less.

### 5. Friends Who Teach Your Fingers to War – Winning the Battle of the Mind - Psalm 144:1
*"Blessed be the LORD my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight."*

Although this verse refers to physical warfare in David's context, believers today also face spiritual battles, many of which begin in the mind. The enemy often attacks through fear, doubt, anxiety, temptation, discouragement, bitterness, lust, pride, and negative thinking. The battlefield is frequently the human mind.

Friends who teach your fingers to war are those who equip you spiritually to overcome these battles. They teach you how to stand on God's Word, pray effectively, recognize the enemy's schemes, and renew your mind according to Scripture.

Romans 12:2 urges believers not to be conformed to this world but to be transformed by the renewing of their minds. Likewise, 2 Corinthians 10:4–5 teaches that spiritual weapons are mighty through God for pulling down strongholds and bringing every thought into obedience to Christ.

**Such friends help you:**
- Replace fear with faith.
- Resist temptation.
- Develop a disciplined prayer life.
- Study God's Word consistently.
- Guard your thoughts against deception.
- Trust God's truth over your emotions.

These are friends who remind you that every spiritual battle is won through dependence on God rather than human strength.

### Conclusion

Friendship is far more than social interaction; it is a divine relationship that shapes our lives, character, and eternal destiny. Every friendship either moves us closer to God's purpose or further away from it.

As believers, we should intentionally cultivate friendships that encourage gratitude, inspire excellence, build godly character, strengthen faith, and prepare us for life's spiritual battles. Equally important, we should strive to become such friends to others.

May God grant us the wisdom to discern healthy relationships, the humility to receive godly correction, and the grace to be faithful companions who reflect the love and character of Christ.

*"A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity."* — **Proverbs 17:17**

title: Depression: Understanding the Silent Battle and Finding Hope
description:
## DEPRESSION: UNDERSTANDING THE SILENT BATTLE AND FINDING HOPE

Depression is one of the most common yet misunderstood challenges affecting people today. It is more than ordinary sadness or disappointment. Depression is a serious condition that can affect a person's emotions, thoughts, physical health, relationships, work, and spiritual life. It is a silent battle that many people fight behind closed doors.

In a society filled with academic stress, family problems, economic pressures, sickness, unemployment, and various uncertainties, many individuals find themselves overwhelmed by feelings of hopelessness and despair.

The good thing is that depression is not a death sentence or end of story, there is hope and healing for those who are enabled to find help in God.

### Depression (Definition)

Depression is a state of prolonged sadness, loss of interest in activities, low self esteem, lack of energy, difficulty coping with daily life and feeling of worthlessness. It is imperative to understand that while everyone experiences sadness occasionally, depression persists for weeks, months or even years if left untreated.

**The signs of depression are:**
- Persistent sadness
- Lack of energy
- Loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities
- Feeling of guilt or worthlessness
- Thoughts of self harm or suicide
- Loss of appetite or overeating, etc.

### Bible Examples of Depression

The Scripture records people who experienced deep emotional distress, among who are:

1. **Elijah** became discouraged and wished to die after facing intense pressure — **1 Kings 19:4**. God responded by giving him rest, food and encouragement.
2. **David** often expressed sorrow and despair, yet he continually placed his hope in God — **Psalm 42:11**.
3. **Job** experienced overwhelming suffering and emotional pain but remained faithful and God eventually restored him. God doesn't leave His own comfortless. — **Job 10:1**.

### The Severe Damages of Depression

- **Spiritual damage:** Weakens prayer life, faith and fellowship with God.
- **Physical damage:** Causes fatigue, sleep disorders, headache and poor health.
- **Emotional damage:** Leads to hopelessness, anxiety, and low self worth.
- **Relationship damage:** Creates isolation and conflicts within families and friendships.
- **Productivity damage:** Reduces concentration, academic performance and work efficiency.
- **Risk of suicide:** Severe depression may result in thoughts of self harm or suicide.

### Way Out

It is important to note that every occurrence in our realm is a resultant effect of an encounter. To rid of it therefore, one would also tune to more superior encounters, hence the below highlights:

1. Pray and cast your burdens on God. — **1 Peter 5:7**
2. Meditate on God's word for strength and hope. — **Psalm 119:105**
3. Stay connected to supportive people and Christian fellowship. — **Galatians 6:2**
4. Seek professional help when necessary.
5. Practice gratitude and positive thinking based on God's promises. — **Jeremiah 29:11**
6. Maintain healthy habits like proper rest, exercise and nutrition.

### Conclusion

Depression is real and can have serious effects on every area of life. However, there is hope through God's grace, the support of others who are trusted, healthy living and professional care when needed. God remains close to the brokenhearted and offers healing, strength and restoration.

*"The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit"* — **Psalm 34:18**

---

**By Chris John**
*New Flow B.C Ayobo*
*The Good Herald Baptist Association*
*Lagos West Baptist Conference*

title: Forty Years of Grace: Celebrating a Legacy of Faith, Fellowship, and Impact
description:
## Forty Years of Grace: Celebrating a Legacy of Faith, Fellowship, and Impact
*"One generation shall commend Your works to another and shall declare Your mighty acts."* — **Psalm 145:4**

Forty years is more than a milestone—it is a testimony. It is the story of God's unwavering faithfulness, His sustaining grace, and His commitment to building lives for His glory. As the Lagos State Baptist Student Fellowship marks four remarkable decades of existence, we pause to reflect with gratitude on a journey that has been shaped by divine providence and the sacrificial labour of countless faithful men and women.

From humble beginnings, the fellowship was birthed with a vision to nurture students in the knowledge of Christ, build disciples who would stand firm in faith, and raise ambassadors of the Kingdom who would influence every sphere of society. Forty years later, that vision continues to bear abundant fruit.

The pages of our history are adorned with stories of transformed lives, fervent prayers, passionate worship, sound biblical teaching, and genuine Christian fellowship. Here, many encountered Christ in a life-changing way. Here, destinies were redirected, callings were discovered, and lifelong convictions were forged. For countless individuals, the fellowship became more than a gathering—it became a spiritual home, a training ground, and a family.

Perhaps one of the greatest testimonies of these forty years is not merely in the events we organized or the programs we hosted, but in the people God has raised through this fellowship. Across churches, campuses, communities, professions, and nations stand men and women whose lives bear the unmistakable imprint of the Lagos State Baptist Student Fellowship. Men and women of spiritual timber and calibre—pastors, missionaries, teachers, professionals, ministry leaders, and faithful disciples—whose influence continues to echo far beyond the walls where they first learned to pray, serve, and grow.

These are the fruits of seeds sown by visionary fathers and mothers who laboured tirelessly, often unseen, believing that investing in young lives was an investment in God's Kingdom. We are privileged beneficiaries of their sacrifices. We stand today because they stood then. We reap today because they sowed faithfully. Their prayers, counsel, discipline, and unwavering commitment have become the foundation upon which successive generations continue to build.

The journey has not been without its challenges. Every generation has faced changing times, evolving cultures, and unique pressures. Yet through every season, the fellowship has remained anchored in the unchanging truth of God's Word. His faithfulness has preserved the vision, strengthened the work, and ensured that His purpose continues to prevail.

As we celebrate forty years, we do so not merely with nostalgia but with renewed commitment. We honour our past because it reminds us of God's faithfulness, but we also embrace the future with expectation. The God who sustained the fellowship through four decades is able to do even greater things in the years ahead. The next chapter calls for a new generation of students and alumni who will cherish this heritage, uphold the values upon which the fellowship was founded, and continue the sacred task of raising disciples for Christ. The baton that has been faithfully carried across forty years must not be dropped. Instead, it must be passed on with even greater conviction, excellence, and passion.

As we commemorate this ruby jubilee, we celebrate not only the years that have passed but the lives that have been transformed, the leaders that have been raised, the souls that have been won, and the countless testimonies that only eternity will fully reveal.

To every pioneer who dared to dream, every pastor who provided guidance, every fellowship executive who served with diligence, every worker who laboured behind the scenes, every alumnus whose prayers and support sustained the vision, and every student who has called this fellowship home—we say thank you. Above all, we return all glory to God, the Author and Sustainer of this remarkable story. For forty years, He has been our Shepherd, our Keeper, our Provider, and our Guide. His faithfulness has never failed. As we celebrate today, we pray that future generations will gather to celebrate even greater testimonies, declaring that the God who began this good work remained faithful to complete it.

**Happy 40th Anniversary to the Lagos State Baptist Student Fellowship.**
**To God alone be all the glory.**

title: The Heart: A Tool of Worship
description:
## AN ARTICLE ON THE HEART: A TOOL OF WORSHIP BY ADERONKE FOWOTADE

**(Director: Irreplaceable Voice Music Ministry Lagos, Nigeria)**

The popular song that reigned in the late 90s written by Matt Redman "When the Music Fades",

*"When the music fades
All is stripped away
And I simply come
Longing just to bring
Something that's of worth
That will bless Your heart
I'll bring You more than a song
For a song in itself
Is not what You have required
You search much deeper within
Through the way things appear
You're looking into my heart
I'm coming back to the heart of worship
And it's all about You,
It's all about You, Jesus
I'm sorry, Lord, for the thing I've made it
When it's all about You,
It's all about You, Jesus"*

It is of noteworthy that worship should be in reverence to God alone because He is the object of our worship and He has created us to show forth His praise. *The relationship between our hearts and expressing our worship is inseparable.*

### Definition of key words

**A TOOL:** A tool is a device or an instrument that is used to conduct a specific task. *A tool in the context of this article is the man that will conduct the assignment of genuine worship to his creator.*

**WORSHIP:** *Worship is an act of valuing and honoring God, expressing our, reverence and total devotion. Worship is a life, and should be lived daily, it is not compartmental living but wholesome living, physical, spiritual, emotional, and psychological.*

### Purpose of worship

**Isaiah 43:21** "This people have I formed for myself; they shall show forth my praise".

**Rev 4:11** "Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created". *These scriptures emphasized why we are created, which is solely to worship God alone.*

### THE HEART AS A TOOL OF WORSHIP

*Why is the heart so important in offering our worship to God?* **Proverbs 4:23** "Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life."

*As Christians we are to be careful of what we store in hearts, because God is Spirit, they that will worship him must worship Him in Spirit and in Truth* **John 4:23**. *His Spirt indwelling will spur us to worship in the exact way He requires that worship to be rendered to Him. The heart cannot be separated from offering quality worship. A man that will worship God must be a man of spiritual discipline.*

*Men like Abraham, David, Paul, Mary the mother of Jesus, The Levites who performed their priestly duties in the temple in the Old Testament era, our Lord Jesus exemplified worship through his prayer life, his teachings, and his obedience to the Father. He also taught his followers the importance of worshipping God in spirit and truth.*

**Romans 12:1-2** "Therefore, I urge you, brothers, and sisters, in view of God’s mercy, to offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God—this is your true and proper worship. 2 Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what God’s will is—his good, pleasing, and perfect will". *To offer an acceptable worship the state of the heart cannot be downplayed hence a man of contrite and broken spirit is the man that his worship will be acceptable before God.*

### ATTITUDES OF TRUE WORSHIP

- Worship is done in total fear and reverence to God.
- Purification, consecration, and sanctification of the heart in readiness to offering of worship.
- God should be the focus of the worship. Its all about Him not us. John 3:30

*In conclusion, to be a tool of worship, your heart must be transformed. A man who does not know God cannot offer an acceptable worship to God, hence it is important that our lives reflect what is pleasing and acceptable unto our maker and you can only do this by constantly engaging the word of God. IT’S ALL ABOUT JESUS.*

### References

- King James Bible
- Online sources
- The Big Worship Box Set Matt Redman (When the Music fades released 2005)
- https://www.biblegateway.com/passage/?search=Romans%2012%3A1-2&version=NIV

title: Finding Ground in Shifting Seasons
description:
## FINDING GROUND IN SHIFTING SEASONS

There is a quiet, uncomfortable space that exists between the end of one chapter and the beginning of the next. It’s the season when the structure of a previous milestone falls away and the grand blueprint for the future is still a blank page.

In these moments, we are often told to "just have faith” but standard advice rarely accounts for how heavy that phrase can feel when the job market is unpredictable or when daily routines feels more like waiting than living.

True faith isn’t a cosmic guarantee that everything will turn out exactly on our preferred timeline. It doesn’t promise a smooth path, it simply anchors us so we don’t lose our footing when the ground moves beneath us.

It’s the quiet, intentional decision to believe that your current position is not your final destination. It’s the bravery to keep showing up, perfecting your craft and choosing patience over panic when the silence feels loud.

This isn’t passive waiting; it is active preparation.

When the big picture feels overwhelming, faith requires us to shrink our focus down to the immediate present. You don’t need to figure out the next five years today. You only need enough light for the next step.

Ultimately, faith is the audacity to look at an uncertain horizon and decide, despite every reason to worry, that you cannot fail. Not because the road will be easy but because you’re entirely capable of navigating the journey.

---

**Esther Ayobami Oluwatimilehin**
Abundant Grace Baptist Association

title: What Has Become of That Altar?
description:
## WHAT HAS BECOME OF THAT ALTAR?
**By Emmanuel O. Okegbemi (InManIsGod)**
*inmanisgod@gmail.com*

**Hosea 8:11 NIV**
**“Though Ephraim built many altars for sin offerings, these have become altars for sinning.”**

Hmm. They were building altars to atone for sin, but instead of receiving answers, they used the altar to multiply sin.

Little do we know that we become what we build.
Little do we know that we become what we say.
Little do we know that we become what we fear.
Little do we know that we become what we are becoming.

We are now creators. We recreate what God has created — through our actions and our inactions.
We run our lives as though we own them, and no one seems to care what damage we do.

What an outcry in the heart of God for His children! What an outburst of anguish for the ones He loves!
But His burden grew heavier because we did not just turn away — we became what we turned to.

If only we would look into the law of liberty and let that become our becoming.
If only we would turn to His Love expressed on the cross, and let that become our becoming.
If only we would turn to His Spirit in us and let that become our becoming.
If only we would look at His face in His Word and in His work.
If only we would pay attention to His voice — at least to His Word.
If only we would see His broken heart in our conscience,
How much better our becoming would have been.

Or will we yet continue with multiple altars when the greatest altar He desires is our heart?
We continue to attend multiple programs when the greatest program He desires is our heartfelt meeting with Him.
We continue to design and structure events, church activities, and others, when our own lives need restructuring.
We continue to make unending speeches when His love has ended in our hearts.

How long will we keep up this charade? And how soon before we turn back to His simple plea?

*“Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded.”* – **James 4:8**

How do you do this, you ask? Hear what Paul says to us in **Romans 12:1**:

*“And so, dear brothers and sisters, I plead with you to give your bodies to God because of all He has done for you. Let them be a living and holy sacrifice—the kind He will find acceptable. This is truly the way to worship Him.”* **[New Living Translation]**

*“My Christian friends, God has been so very good and kind to us. That is the reason why I am asking you very strongly to offer your bodies to Him. Bring your bodies to Him, as a sacrifice that is still alive. Give yourselves to Him completely, so that He may be happy because of you. That is how you can really worship God.”* **[EasyEnglish]**

*“So, here’s what I want you to do, with God helping you: Take your everyday, ordinary life—your sleeping, eating, going-to-work, and walking-around life—and place it before God as an offering. Embracing what God does for you is the best thing you can do for Him.”* **[Message]**

Beloved, He will not keep this access open forever, and neither will the devil stay silent for long.
He will not be patient forever, and neither will the devil give men room to keep adjusting.
But as long as it is still now — I cannot guarantee tomorrow.

How long will you multiply the altar of sin and become it?

Let today be the day you make that deliberate decision to be intentional in your relationship with God. Let it be the day you repair your personal altar and make room for Him. Let it be the time you give your life to consistent study of the Word, a deliberate life of prayer, and a consistent willingness to yield to God’s instructions.

When you are not building an altar of relationship with God, you are definitely building an altar unto sin.

So how do we turn back — especially in this age where everything moves too fast and everything screams for our attention?

### 1. Stop.
Not tomorrow. Not “after this project/program.” Now. The speed of this age is not an excuse; it is the very reason to pause. Daniel purposed in his heart *in Babylon*. You can purpose in your heart right where you are. Do not postpone it.

### 2. Strip.
Strip the altar down. Delete the app. End the relationship. Cancel the routine. Return the money. Confess the lie. Leave that cohabitation or that friend's house that is not pleasing to God. Altars unto sin survive on what we refuse to tear down. *“Tear down your father’s altar to Baal”* — **Judges 6:25**. What’s your father’s altar?

### 3. Stay.
Rebuild by remaining. Ten minutes in the Word before you touch your phone. Five minutes of worship song before you watch that movie. A sincere “God, speak” before you speak. Start little and it gets better. This is how you repair the altar in a distracted age — not with 12-hour vigils once a month that you even find hard to keep, but with daily, deliberate moments you will.

### 4. Submit.
You cannot do this alone. Distraction is a spirit and a system. If you have decided to turn, tell someone today. A believer. Your pastor. A mature friend. Isolation is the devil’s fastest route to relapse.

Beloved, the altar will not repair itself. The age will not slow down for you. But *you* can slow down for God.

*“Return to Me,” says the Lord of hosts, “and I will return to you.”* – **Zechariah 1:3**

Let today be the day. Not after the sermon. Not next year. Today.

If you have made that decision, do not walk it alone. Reach out now. Send the text. Make the call. Enter the room. Be accountable to someone that keeps you responsible to your altar.

The greatest altar He desires is waiting: your heart.

**Shalom.**
author: Emmanuel O. Okegbemi

title: The Spirit of Excellence
description:
## TOPIC: THE SPIRIT OF EXCELLENCE.

Many students live in a dilemma of what excellence is supposed to mean. Is it meant to be owning house, cars or just being the richest. In **Philippians 4:8**, Apostle Paul advises us as Christians to think about lovely, pure, true, admirable, praiseworthy and **EXCELLENT** things. The mind and thought of God for us as believers is to be Excellent in all ramifications of our lives.

Just like Daniel in the book of **Daniel Chapter 1**. Daniel had the spirit of excellence which made him able to understand what his peers and even a king could not comprehend. Excellence involves balancing Educational, spiritual, moral, social and financial lifestyle.

### WHAT IS THE SPIRIT OF EXCELLENCE?

The spirit we call excellence is the manifestation of high standards and giving out your best beyond a counterpart expectations. The spirit involves morals and values such as:

- Consistency
- Determination
- Integrity
- Growth mindset
- Discipline and many more.

Daniel was able to prove the existence of God with the determination and discipline he had to be the excellent legend we all should emulate Today.

### HOW DOES THE SPIRIT OF EXCELLENCE WORK?

**1. Being rooted in our identity as a Christian (1 Peter 2:9):** And we are chosen, called out of many thousands and a royal priesthood. Living with the understanding that kings don't fail activates the inborn spirit of excellence.

**2. Empowered by the Holy Spirit (Galatians 5:22-23):** The spirit produces diligence, self control, faithfulness. We don't have to white-knuckle excellence. We walk in the spirit and the Holy Ghost manifests excellence.

**3. Motivated by love, not fear (2 Timothy 1:7):** For the Lord has not given any of us the spirit of fear but of love, power and of a sound mind. Excellence isn't to earn God's love but it is a response to the love of God. We are expected to give our best back.

### BENEFITS OF THE MANIFESTATION OF THE SPIRIT OF EXCELLENCE

- God will entrust you with more assignments.
- You become a tool and a vessel of honor unto God.
- It is the mind of God for every believer to Excel.
- Excellence is a proof of purposeful living.

In conclusion, the spirit of excellence is not perfectionism, not pride, neither is it burn out. But in all God is the sufficient provider of wisdom and wisdom is profitable to direct.
author: Refreshing 2026 Editorial

title: Camp Rules & Regulations
description:
## CAMP RULES & REGULATIONS

1. Registration is compulsory for all campers without exception; even if you are staying for only a single night on the camp premises.
2. Official name tags must be worn and kept visible at all times.
3. Ensure you keep your tags safe; they will serve as the strictly enforced pass for entry and collection of food. Failure to produce your tag will meet consequences.
4. No camper may leave the campground without explicit permission from the Camp Coordinators.
5. All participants must obey instructions at designated security checkpoints.
6. Campers are expected to display Christ-like behavior, respect all leaders, and honor God in words and actions.
7. Disrespect, gossiping, fighting, bullying, or any violent behavior will not be tolerated under any circumstances.
8. Attendance and promptness are mandatory for all camp activities.
9. Campers must bring their Bibles, notebooks, and writing materials to sessions.
10. Dress modestly, decently, and in accordance with Christian values at all times.
   - **Boys:** No sagging, earrings, or sleeveless tops.
   - **Girls:** Skirts must be knee-length or longer. No crop tops, see-through, or tight-fitting clothes.
11. Male and female campers are strictly forbidden from entering each other’s hostels or rooms.
12. Report all illnesses or injuries immediately to the Camp Health Officer.
13. Report any suspicious activity or missing items to the Secretariat immediately.
author: Refreshing 2026 Planning Committee

let the earth hear his voice!

let the people rejoice!

O perfect redemption, the purchase of blood!
To ev'ry believer the promise of God;

but purer and higher and greater will be
